title: Ballot Buddy · New Jersey

boxes.title: How to read this
boxes.html: This report does not tell you who to vote for. It lays out who wrote the checks and what the public record shows. A donation is a fact about the donor; it is not proof of what the candidate will do.

footer: Sources. Who ran and who won: the Nov 3, 2026 results in the Results tab. Federal money: FEC bulk files, downloaded Nov 2, 2026. Records and positions: linked per item. New Jersey state-race money isn't in the guide yet, so those candidates have no money meters.

races.title: U.S. Senate
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Justin Murphy

pacs: New Jersey Right To Life Committee Federal PAC
outside: NEW JERSEY RIGHT TO  LIFE COMMITTEE FEDERAL PAC
money.note: Individuals gave $56,781; PAC money $2,570; candidate's own money $4,932. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Republican and U.S. Navy veteran from New Jersey who is self-employed. He has served as Deputy Mayor of Tabernacle. He ran in the 2024 Republican U.S. Senate primary, finishing third with 11.3%, and won the 2026 Republican primary.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Justin Murphy was born or raised, or when he moved to New Jersey. We found no details on his Navy service, his self-employed business, or when he served as Deputy Mayor of Tabernacle and whether the post was elected. We found no statements from him on data centers, homestead property tax relief, limits on institutional or foreign buyers of homes and land, or teacher pay. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, and no endorsements or controversies were documented in the pages reviewed. The campaign website text was cut off near the end.

workers-first.evidence: Says he supports Section 287(g) so state and local police can take part in immigration enforcement, wants federal aid withheld from sanctuary jurisdictions, and wants a visa system that can track visa holders including students.

back-police-order.evidence: Says crime can be reduced by securing the border, deporting criminal aliens, and bringing federal charges when state and local prosecutors fail to enforce criminal codes.

second-amendment.evidence: Pledges to oppose any attempt to restrict the right to bear arms and says he supports Constitutional Carry.

pro-life.evidence: Says life begins at conception and opposes tax dollars funding abortion. He supports parental notification, a ban on partial-birth abortion and pro-adoption policies. He allows exceptions for the life of the mother, rape and incest, which is narrower than a ban with no exceptions.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Says he supports school choice and would abolish the federal Department of Education, dividing its budget among local school boards for public school funding and voucher programs. His pledge does not mention teacher pay.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Says that as a senator he wants the NJ Pinelands kept pristine and the Jersey Shore kept free of pollution and windmills, and lists protecting land and shores as a priority.

prio.label: Matches 6 of 6 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 6 only promised

cands.name: Cory Booker

money.note: Individuals gave $15,675,001; PAC money $512,780; candidate's own money $0. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: U.S. senator from New Jersey since 2013. Yale-trained lawyer and former Rhodes Scholar. Worked as a staff attorney for the Urban Justice Center, served on the Newark Municipal Council (1998–2002), and was mayor of Newark (2006–2013). Ran for president in 2020 and suspended his campaign in January 2020.

controversies.text: Federal records show $5,000 from AIPAC's PAC since 2021; $708,680 from individuals passed through that PAC in 2025-26.
Missed 40 of 915 U.S. Senate votes this Congress (4.4%), counted from the roll calls through 2026-09-30. Longest run of misses: 7, 2026-06-16 to 2026-06-17.

In a February 2012 radio interview, Mayor Booker said Newark's unemployment rate fell 2 points in the past year. His office backed this with real federal data comparing January to December 2011, which were not seasonally adjusted. PolitiFact rated it False because the December-to-December drop was 0.7 points. His office called the statement accurate.

cands.gaps: We found no documented positions or actions from Booker on data centers, homestead property tax relief, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, growth and land conservation, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay in the pages we could read. We found no record of him backing police pay or pension measures. The pages did not show his earlier work in detail, including any development decisions as Newark mayor. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, so we have no questionnaire answers from him. The Ballotpedia page was cut off partway through its list of past key votes, and the Wikipedia page was cut off in its Senate tenure section.

clean-money.evidence: His campaign site says he does not accept money from federal lobbyists, corporate PACs, or fossil fuel and pharma executives, and describes the campaign as powered by grassroots supporters.

workers-first.evidence: Voted Nay on the Laken Riley Act (S.5), which required DHS to detain certain unlawfully present immigrants arrested for theft-related offenses; the bill passed the Senate 64-35 in 2025.

second-amendment.evidence: Voted Nay on H.J.Res. 44, a resolution to nullify the ATF rule on firearms with stabilizing braces; the resolution failed 50-49 in the Senate.

platform.summary: This is the platform Ballot Buddy scores against, adapted to New Jersey. James Fishback ran on it in the 2026 Republican primary for Florida governor: an affordability and land-protection message on top of a conservative base. Details that only applied to Florida have been swapped for New Jersey. It's one yardstick, chosen by this guide, and not a neutral one.

planks.title: Ban data centers statewide
planks.promise: Ban AI and hyperscale data centers in every New Jersey county through statewide preemption of county approvals, to protect farmland, water and electric bills.
planks.tells_for: Votes or stated positions to ban, put a moratorium on, or preempt data-center approvals; opposing data-center rezonings on farmland; refusing data-center-industry money.
planks.tells_against: Votes to approve or fast-track a data center, rezone farmland for one, or give it tax breaks; campaigning on attracting data centers or AI infrastructure.

planks.title: Eliminate homestead property taxes
planks.promise: Eliminate property taxes on New Jersey residents' primary homes (not second homes, short-term rentals or mega-estates), paid for by rolling local government spending back.
planks.tells_for: Votes for homestead exemption increases, assessment caps or abolition; pledges to cut or end homestead taxes; pledges to cut local spending or tax rates.
planks.tells_against: Votes or statements for raising property taxes; opposing homestead tax relief; defending local government revenue growth.

planks.title: New Jersey homes and land for New Jerseyans
planks.promise: Ban private equity and Wall Street firms from buying single-family homes, tax out-of-state vacation-home buyers, and keep foreign adversaries from owning New Jersey land.
planks.tells_for: Supporting limits on institutional or foreign buyers of homes and land; proposing taxes or caps on out-of-state or investor purchases.
planks.tells_against: Opposing limits on corporate or foreign land buying; courting institutional or foreign real-estate capital.

planks.title: Slow growth, protect land and water
planks.promise: Develop slower and smarter, stop overdevelopment, and conserve New Jersey's state parks, waterways and natural lands.
planks.tells_for: Votes or statements to hold or tighten growth limits, require approvals for large developments, deny rezonings of farmland or open space, fund conservation; refusing developer money.
planks.tells_against: Votes to expand development boundaries, waive development oversight, preempt local growth limits, approve large developer land deals over resident objections; heavy developer funding.

planks.title: New Jersey workers first: end H-1B
planks.promise: End H-1B abuse with fines that wipe out any savings from replacing a New Jersey worker, keep H-1B workers off state contracts, raise foreign-student tuition, and back strong immigration enforcement and deportations.
planks.tells_for: Votes or statements for state cooperation with federal immigration enforcement, E-Verify, detention of criminal illegal immigrants, limiting H-1B or guest-worker displacement of Americans.
planks.tells_against: Votes or statements against immigration-enforcement bills; defending H-1B or guest-worker expansion or sanctuary-style policies.

planks.title: No foreign or big-donor money
planks.promise: Refuse contributions from foreign-affiliated groups (naming AIPAC) and run against donor capture.
planks.tells_for: Stated pledges to refuse foreign-linked, corporate-PAC, developer or out-of-state big-donor money; small-dollar funded campaigns.
planks.tells_against: Documented reliance on developer, foreign-linked or mega-donor or PAC money; stated openness to it.

planks.title: Back police, restore order
planks.promise: Raise pay and improve pensions for law enforcement and corrections officers, charge teen takeovers as felonies, surge state resources on homelessness, and remove prosecutors who refuse to prosecute.
planks.tells_for: Votes or positions raising penalties for rioting or disorder, funding or improving pay and pensions for officers, supporting police, tough-on-crime prosecution.
planks.tells_against: Votes cutting officer pensions or benefits; opposing penalties for public disorder; defund-style positions.

planks.title: Defend the Second Amendment
planks.promise: Eliminate Red Flag laws, end restrictions on suppressors, bump stocks and forced-reset triggers, and oppose raising gun purchase ages; also pull Flock cameras and stop Palantir contracts.
planks.tells_for: Votes for permitless carry and stand-your-ground, against red-flag laws and new purchase-age limits; pledges to oppose new gun restrictions.
planks.tells_against: Votes for red-flag laws, purchase-age or waiting-period laws, assault-weapon or magazine limits.

planks.title: Pro-life, no exceptions
planks.promise: Life begins at conception; shut down New Jersey's abortion clinics and replace them with crisis pregnancy centers, plus paid maternity leave.
planks.tells_for: Votes or statements for abortion bans, waiting periods or other abortion restrictions; support for pregnancy centers.
planks.tells_against: Votes or statements against abortion restrictions; support for abortion-access measures.

planks.title: School choice and teacher pay
planks.promise: Universal school choice funded toward parity with public schools, a state homeschool commissioner, and a 25% raise for teachers.
planks.tells_for: Votes or statements for vouchers, charters or universal choice and for raising teacher pay.
planks.tells_against: Votes or statements against voucher or charter expansion or school-choice funding.
